Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.8% today, extending a steep two-week decline of 11%, as crude oil prices dropped sharply on reports that Iran and the U.S. conflict may be de-escalating. Brent crude fell below $90 a barrel—the lowest since August—after President Trump suggested the conflict would end "fairly soon," reducing the geopolitical risk premium that had been supporting energy prices. For a refiner, lower crude prices are a mixed bag: while cheaper oil sounds good, it compresses profit margins because refined products (gasoline, diesel) fall in lockstep, and the company loses the benefit of selling expensive fuel into a tight market.

The broader backdrop matters here too. Even as crude tumbled, refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and crude inventories remain elevated at nearly 692 million barrels, signaling ample supply and weak demand relative to production. A political shift favoring renewables after recent elections also clouds the longer-term outlook for traditional refining demand, adding to near-term pricing pressure on the stock.
